title: High heels were made for men
hook: High heels were first worn by men, and they started on horseback.
peek: Heels began as riding gear for Persian horsemen, helping their feet stay in the stirrups. In the 1600s European aristocrats copied them, and for a while the most fashionable heels in Europe belonged to men.
lede: Historians of footwear, notably Elizabeth Semmelhack of Toronto's Bata Shoe Museum, trace the heel to West Asia, especially Persia, where riders wore heeled shoes to keep their feet steady in the stirrups. Around 1600, contact with Persia sparked a fashion for Persian things in Europe, and aristocratic men began wearing heels. They were impractical for walking, which was partly the point.

bullets.text: The French king wore shoes with red heels, and at his court red heels became a mark of privilege. His official portraits show them clearly.

In the 1600s fashionable women in Europe began adopting touches of men's dress, and heels were among them, as Semmelhack has described. Over time women's heels grew slimmer while men's stayed broad and sturdy.
In 1930 the psychologist J. C. Flügel used this phrase for the way European men gave up showy dress around 1800. Men's heels had already faded during the 1700s, and heels became mainly women's wear.
The riding heel never fully left. Western riding boots still have a raised heel for the same reason Persian riders did: it stops the foot sliding through the stirrup.
